texts: The calcified left ventricular mass involving the papillary muscles in this child is a fibroma, and the best management is partial resection of the mass: D.
Fibromas are firm, often calcified and do not regress; removing most of the tumour relieves the obstruction and the arrhythmias, even when the part woven into the papillary muscles must be left.
In the picture, Zoro carves away most of the chalky lump and leaves the part wrapped round the pillars that hold the harp strings.
Medicines do not shrink a fibroma, anticoagulation does not treat it, and autotransplantation or heart transplantation is kept for tumours that cannot be dealt with otherwise.
Memory hook: carve away the chalky lump, but leave what grips the pillars.
